answer: Each identity registers one seal carved from one jade blank, its face cut with a unique 14-groove sonnet sequence, filed before first use. Verification is optical: light shone through the seal throws a diffuse nebula fixed by groove geometry and fibrous structure, so a resin copy scatters differently and fails. Carving is subtractive: grooves are cut singly, three hours per seal, and hurried cuts crack jade along its grain, ruining the blank. An honest agent commissions one seal; 1,000 identities need 1,000 blanks and 3,000 carver-hours, since one nebula certifies only its registered sequence.
